chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about a man who prays behind an Imam and does not know how many rak'ahs he has prayed; is there any negligence (sahw) upon him? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.سَهْوٌ: Negligence or inadvertent error in worship

ai.seo_question: Does a worshipper incur negligence (sahw) if they are unsure how many rak'ahs they prayed behind the Imam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), the concept of *sahw* (negligence penalty) is clarified for a follower praying behind an Imam who is unaware of the exact number of rak'ahs completed. The ruling that no penalty is incurred reflects the Shia principle of ease (*taysir*) in worship, distinguishing between intentional error and genuine uncertainty (*shakk*) in congregational settings. This hadith is foundational in *tahdhib al-ahkam* for establishing that the validity of the prayer is not compromised by the follower's lack of precise count when following the Imam's lead.
